subject: Usage input not available for polygon detectors

messages.author: c4391c6727fe6d94
messages.subject: Usage input not available for polygon detectors
parts:
Hi all,


So I'm trying to estimate the abundance of a population of stray dogs in multiple different spatial sessions (sites). Each spatial session is made up of an array of grid cells (polygons) which were surveyed using a search-encounter method. Of the 12 sites, 5 were surveyed twice, while the others were surveyed 4 times. 

Therefore, I attempted to use the usage column in my detector files to denote the number of times each site was surveyed. Polygons in sites that were surveyed twice had a usage input of 1100 while polygons in sites that were surveyed 4 times had a usage input of 1111. However, when I tried to compile the trap data with read.traps(), I got this error:

"usage input not available for polygon detectors in 4.4"

Also, I have the xy coordinates and covariates of my custom habitat mask for each site in .csv files. Is it possible to just enter all the data in my .csv files as a single list in R with something like read.table() and then use that list in secr.fit()?


Cheers,
Josh

messages.author: c4391c6727fe6d94
messages.subject: Re: Usage input not available for polygon detectors
parts:
Hi,

I still need help with using the usage input for my polygons, but I think I have figured how to enter my custom habitat masks into R. I am sure there's a much better way to do it (I'm not even sure if I'm doing it right), but here's what I did:

Step 1: Read all my csv files into R
ssdf1 <- read.csv("ssdf1.csv")
ssdf2 <- read.csv("ssdf2.csv")
ssdf3 <- read.csv("ssdf3.csv")
.
.
.

Step 2: Extract the first two columns which contain the xy coordinates
mask1 <- ssdf1[ , 1:2]
mask2 <- ssdf2[ , 1:2]
mask3 <- ssdf3[ , 1:2]
.
.
.

Step 3: Extract the columns which contain the covariates
cov1 <- ssdf1[ , 3:10]
cov2 <- ssdf2[ , 3:10]
cov3 <- ssdf3[ , 3:10]
.
.
.

Step 4: Coerce the data in step 2 to become habitat masks that are recognized by secr
hab_mask1 <- make.mask(mask1, buffer=375, spacing=750, type="trapbuffer")
hab_mask2 <- make.mask(mask2, buffer=375, spacing=750, type="trapbuffer")
hab_mask3 <- make.mask(mask3, buffer=375, spacing=750, type="trapbuffer")
.
.
.
(The space between the center xy coordinates of each of my polygons is 750m, so to retain the correct coordinates of the habitat mask, I defined my buffer to be half of the spacing)

Step 5: Add the covariates to the habitat masks created in step 4
covariates(hab_mask1) <- cov1
covariates(hab_mask2) <- cov2
covariates(hab_mask3) <- cov3
.
.
.

After this, I think all I have to is define my habitat mask in secr.fit() as a list of all my habitat masks. It would be helpful if I could have some confirmation if what I did was correct (I still can't run secr.fit() due to another problem which I talk about in another conversation). I have attached the csv files just in case.

Cheers,
Josh
